items.text: I understand what a shell is and how it sits between the user and the OS
I can explain the difference between GUI and CLI with examples
I know why CLI is preferred for cloud server management
I understand what EC2 is and can explain it as IaaS
I can describe what an AMI is and what it contains
I can explain the five EC2 instance type families and when to use each
I understand how key pair authentication works (public key on EC2, private key on laptop)
I can explain what a Security Group does and the difference between inbound and outbound rules
I understand what EBS is and how it relates to EC2 storage
I can log into the AWS console, select a region, and navigate to EC2
I can launch an EC2 instance: select AMI, instance type, key pair, and security group
I can create a key pair and download the private key file
I can SSH into a Linux EC2 instance from Windows Command Prompt
I can install software on EC2 using yum and start/stop services
I can terminate an EC2 instance to stop charges
I know EC2 = IaaS, the default username for Amazon Linux (ec2-user), and free tier instance (t2.micro)
I can recall SSH port (22), HTTP port (80), and HTTPS port (443)
I know Security Groups are stateful and can explain what that means
I can correctly identify where the public key and private key are stored
I know the two private key formats (.pem and .ppk) and which tools use each
